subject.title: fix(agents): apply stale-run liveness check to aborted subagent orphan recovery

question: Should interrupted-recovery terminal ownership remain the persisted `terminalOwner` state, or should the same guarantees be represented through current main's newer lifecycle primitives?
rationale: The conflicted files independently changed persistence, restart replay, cooperative suspension, provider completion, yield, cleanup, and task projection, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent ownership representation.

options.title: Use current-main primitives
options.body: Translate the branch's exact-run durability, retry, and late-callback guarantees into the newer canonical lifecycle structures without adding a parallel terminal path.

options.title: Retain `terminalOwner`
options.body: Keep the persisted marker if current main has no equivalent closed ownership state and validate its normalization across upgrades and restart.

options.title: Create a replacement PR
options.body: Preserve the tests and proof in a narrow current-main branch if safe integration would require rewriting most of this branch.

recommendation.title: Use current-main primitives
recommendation.body: Translate the branch's exact-run durability, retry, and late-callback guarantees into the newer canonical lifecycle structures without adding a parallel terminal path.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the branch ownership model and current-main changes in the conflicting paths and are assigned to this PR.
